headline: New Mexico Halts New Uranium Mining on 13 Million Acres
meta_description: New Mexico bans new uranium mining on over 13 million acres of state trust lands and commits to cleaning up abandoned mining sites.
summary_short: New Mexico has banned new uranium mining across more than 13 million acres of state trust lands, shifting focus toward remediation of abandoned sites.
body:
New Mexico has banned new uranium mining on more than 13 million acres of state trust lands. The decision marks a significant shift in how the state will manage its mineral-rich public lands.

Beyond the mining freeze, New Mexico's Land Office has been ordered to prioritize the cleanup of abandoned uranium sites left behind by decades of mining operations. These forgotten locations have posed environmental and health risks to communities across the state, many with legacies stretching back generations.

The move reflects growing recognition that the cost of restoring damaged land often exceeds the short-term economic gain from extraction. By redirecting resources toward remediation rather than new development, New Mexico is addressing a backlog of environmental liabilities while protecting vast tracts of public land for future generations.
quick_facts: More than 13 million acres of state trust lands affected
New uranium mining banned on New Mexico state lands
Land Office ordered to prioritize cleanup of abandoned sites
Decades of mining left environmental legacy across state
